a.text: Endless reports.
An avalanche of intel has flooded this lonely battleship ever since it left Norport.
There are signs of trouble from Leithanien to the east, Sargon to the southwest, Kjerag to the west... while everything remains silent in the south.
The messages are suffocating, eating away at my nerves.
My mother seems utterly unmoved, impassively issuing order after order.
But even she cannot resist a frown when she reads the 'congratulations' from her fellow dukes.
This is her life.
She is here, and so this is my Lynncardine.
I am home.
Focus, Delphine. Listen to the reports. This is no time to let your mind wander.
She adjusts the position of her eye patch. Is it to hide the wrinkles?
The weather here is very different from Lynncardine. It's suppressed, heavy, the gloom of rain and fog ever present.
I just want to—

steps.text: What are you gazing at so absent-mindedly, Delphine?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Nothing, Mother.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: It's just...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I don't get to see Londinium from this angle very often.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: I know how you look when your mind is wandering.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Are you bored by the chatters from the rear?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: No... I'm just thinking about Norport Borough.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Sorry, I didn't expect the situation in Londinium to deteriorate so much, so quickly.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: I should have arranged for your evacuation sooner.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: We had compiled reports on everything that went on in Londinium, but we weren't able to bring them.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: We should be the ones apologizing.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: That's alright. A few little troubles don't mean much to the big picture.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Perhaps the Duke of Caster should be held responsible for most of them.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: I know. Let's hope my Messenger isn't making things too difficult for her right now.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: But the value of that intel to subsequent operations...

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Pales in comparison to your value, Delphine. Relax.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: I'm here, and Irnclad Galavae is nearby. Everything will be right again once we return to the city.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: We'll restore Londinium, and Victoria.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Mother, I...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I thought I would die down there.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: I wouldn't let that happen to my daughter.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: You've done well. You have the patience and attention to detail of your father.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: But you don't have to be the one to do all that work. You're my heir, and your place is at Lynncardine.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Our standoff with Leithanien can be trying. You'll need to get used to those matters. Plus... I could use someone to talk to.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I thought I could do better.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: ...Sorry.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: There are many things that a Duke of Windermere must worry about, for which she needs nerves of steel.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: But that's not your burden. Not yet.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: You can rely on your mother, at least until she's too old to walk.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I understand... thank you, mother.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: We'll be home in another four or five hours. I've arranged for all the stuff you left behind at the old house to be set up.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Your pajamas, your pillow, your bed, your bathtub.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: That's all stuff from before I came to Londinium—

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: It's not like you're any taller.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: I have some nice things for you as well, but I'll keep those a secret for now.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Get a good night's sleep once we're back.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: But don't get complacent. We have a lot to do.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I was in Londinium a long time, wasn't I?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I had many friends. Outstanding friends, from whom I had a lot to learn.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: We lived in a city in disorder, chewing up and swallowing the lives we once had. But we believed in our cause. I was proud of it.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Then... things changed. One agent after another disappeared, and the Sarkaz took the city...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I was on my own. I had to live with more... common people. For the first time, I learned how they lived, and how they viewed Victoria.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Most of them are dead now. Those who still live huddle in the bowels of this ship, waiting for you to decide their fate.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: One hundred meters beneath my pajamas, bed, and bathtub.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Hmm.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I'm really grateful, really, but is it all because—

a.text: She does not let me finish.
She puts her hand on my head without patting it, but I know this is her way of showing affection.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: You did well, my daughter. You exceeded my expectations.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Go and see the troops below. It'll do you good to talk with them.

a.text: With that, Her Grace departs. She's always swift and decisive. I have no chance to say any more.
I scratch my slightly untidy head.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Mother!

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: We can talk later.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: You shouldn't have come here yourself!

a.text: The words that come out of my own mouth surprise me.
Was it not because of my call for help that she came?
How could I say that.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: It's too... risky!

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: We can't fully trust the Leithanians, and we don't know what the Sarkaz are planning next!

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: We've fallen behind on intel—

a.text: She dismisses me with a wave, perhaps telling me not to think too much about it.
Her silhouette remains sharp, making me feel like I'm worrying too much, and that she can take handle it all.
Sigh. She's right.
I'm not much taller at all.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: How long will our food last?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I don't think this warship was prepared to take on so many refugees.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: We can't just leave 'em to fend for themselves!

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Mrs. Emil grabbed my hand just now. She didn't say nuffin'. All she did was look at me...

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: I... I can't take it anymore. Let's find Delphine!

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Calm down, Hannah. We're on someone else's ship.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: I just—

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: I'll go keep 'em company. The old timers will feel better with a familiar face around.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I'll stay with you.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Sorry to keep you waiting. I talked to the quartermaster.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Some food will make it to those who need it most... that's the best I can do.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Thank you, Delphine, and thanks to Duke Windermere.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Part of me hopes that Mother really wants to help these poor people out of the kindness of her heart, but...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I know. It's because of me, or should I say, because of who I am.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: It's fine, as long as it helps the people who fled with us.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: You've adapted quickly, Vina.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: The time when we could do as we pleased has passed, Delphine.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Many souls on this ship are counting on me. I have a responsibility to them, both as Vina and as the Siege.

a.text: Lots of people are looking at us. I can tell Vina is busy.
Mother's ship is one of the biggest of the Victorian ships-of-the-line, but it was never designed to evacuate civilians. Certainly not this many.
The people of Norport are squeezed into holds meant to store ammunition and weapons, trying their best to find a clean place to sit down.
This is not the best accommodation, even if the most dangerous weapons have been removed. Vina's gang are doing their best to maintain order.
The refugees whisper about her amongst themselves. The officers on the ship pay no heed, nor does Vina respond to their calls of 'Your Majesty' or 'Your Royal Highness'.
Regardless, she has become the heart and soul of this place.

Perhaps the civilians don't even realize themselves, but the reason they trust Vina is not so much because of her status, but because she is the only one they can rely on in this unfamiliar environment.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: How goes the war?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: The number of reports coming in is unreal. Too many variables to keep track of.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: The Duke of Wellington's offensive is unsteady, and our own defensive lines are being pressed...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: We should have an overwhelming advantage in terms of forces, even if the dukes have yet to commit their full strength. We are facing a foe beyond the scope of modern military theory.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: The Nachzehrer King... the only thing we know about him comes from sparse records of ancient times.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: It has been too long since Victoria, indeed Terra as a whole, last faced a real Sarkaz army.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: What chain reaction will their witchcraft produce? Are they really as primitive and backwards as the records say?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: What force have the various Sarkaz branches come together to form, where we can't see them? Why do they stand together?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: No need to worry too much, though. Mother... Duke Windermere and Duke Wellington will conduct this war together.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: The Duke of Caster has also publicly declared her allegiance. The stalemate will not last long.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Once we return to Irnclad Galavae, both supplies and support will—

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Whoa! What was that?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Looks like we're passing through a canyon... a good thing. It means we're about to leave the battlefield.

a.text: A canyon.
I feel even less at ease.
I know where mother's confidence comes from. This ship is defended by Windermere's pride, her Swordguards.
If the Sarkaz think this merely a reckless act by the Duke of Windermere, they will find themselves on the receiving end of blades that have been honed since the War of the Four Emperors.
But do we truly know the Sarkaz?

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Is the ship slowing down, Siege?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I think so. And the weather outside... say, what time is it?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: How long has it been since we left Norport?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: A few hours, I think.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Is this just an ordinary canyon?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Yes, nothing remarkable besides some abandoned factories...

a.text: Abandoned factories. Yes, this place has been abandoned since before Londinium fell into chaos.
Why? Because of Catastrophe.
The massive crystal formations that Catastrophe left behind...

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Be careful!

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Hey, I'm talking to you!

a.text: Something's not right.
There's a different smell in the air.
I look around instinctively. All the elite soldiers in the hold are gone.
This is not right!

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Get away from him, Hannah!

a.text: Siege pulls her back before I can.
I see the soldier smiling at me.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Look out!

a.text: It's too late.
Blood seeps from the gaps in the ceiling, dripping into the infiltrator's eyes.
Drip.
Merge.
Spread.
Blood?
Where did this blood come from?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Look out!

a.text: Siege pushes me away. An instant later, a blood mist bursts where I stood.
Soon, the entire hold is engulfed in crimson.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Blood mist? Sarkaz witchcraft!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Too many civilians here.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Morgan, Dagda, Indra.

a.text: The four of them exchange gazes, and take up positions around the frightened crowd.
The emotions in the crowd ranges from shock to panic. Some in the corners begin to scream, without even seeing exactly what happened.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Go down! The stairs are to the north!

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Lady Delphine!

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Are you the ship's doctor?

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: We're under attack by witchcraft. The ship's casters can't decipher it yet. The Duke and—

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Damn, how did they—

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Look out!

a.text: A claw slaps away the sword that was inches from his throat.
The blood mist disperses, then reconverges, taking a gooey, wet form.
A Sarkaz emerges from the bloody shadow.

steps.name: Confessarius Guard
steps.text: (In Sarkaz) The Vampire's witchcraft has taken hold.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: I know that outfit... the skull mask...

steps.name: Confessarius Guard
steps.text: (In Sarkaz) The Sighs of Kings... one variable to eliminate.

steps.name: Confessarius Guard
steps.text: (In Sarkaz) Cause chaos and eliminate the outblood. Hesitate not to spill your own blood.

steps.name: Confessarius Guard
steps.text: (In Sarkaz) Oh?

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: You were part of the siege of the Knights of the Tower...

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Careful! I've gotcha!

steps.name: Confessarius Guard
steps.text: (In Sarkaz) You will die here with your king, Victorian.

steps.name: Confessarius Guard
steps.text: (In Sarkaz) Do it.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: (Mother is on deck, but we still have civilians and our people below... I...)

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Delphine! Your left!

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Ugh!

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Careful.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Sorry, thanks.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: There aren't many of them. We can pin them down. The reinforced compartment is one bulkhead away. Get the civilians there—

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: No, there's something more important that you must do.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Those people came with me. I promised to protect them.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Duke Windermere likely doesn't know how bad things are below.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Go and inform her. I'll hold out until your reinforcements arrive.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: But I—

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: This suits us better. You have a formal command structure. There's no way to integrate us quickly.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Vina...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Go!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Damn, you've got a hard head. Almost made my hand go numb.

steps.name: Confessarius Guard
steps.text: *Sarkaz profanity*...

steps.name: Confessarius Guard
steps.text: (In Sarkaz) So be it. The Sighs of Kings will be spoils enough.

steps.name: Confessarius Guard
steps.text: (In Sarkaz) Surround the Aslan.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Get ready for a brawl, mates.

a.text: For an instant, I wished I was with them.
Like when I first joined Slobberknocker Gym, when I went from being alone to being in a community.
Cador, and... Baird.
We stood together.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: This ends now.

a.text: The swing of the hammer compresses the air in the passage. It roars.
Tiny drops of liquid fall on my face.
My vision blurs.

steps.text: Delphine!

a.text: A shadow draws near.

steps.text: Delphine!

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Mother?

a.text: I try to wipe my eyes.
I see another pair of eyes right there in front of me.
Red flows from their sockets.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: Delphine... go no further...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: You're hurt—

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: You'll only be in the way. Same for me.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: Kill me, before whatever this is consumes me.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: The Swordguards and Her Grace will kill the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: Do not put yourself in danger, Delphine... no...

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: I don't even feel the pain anymore...

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: Free me. Then stop.

a.text: I draw my sword.
She is still conscious. I should not do this to her. But I see the relief in her eyes.
She grabs my sword, sending it into her own body.
I'm trembling. I can't see clearly.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: Lady Delphine—You must live—

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: Thank you—for freeing me—

a.text: I look down and see the red eyes.
She gives up breathing, smiling to the end.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: This is... Sarkaz...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Mother...

a.text: My feet cannot move. Worry, unease, and fear grip them.
The lights go out. The only light comes from above deck.
There is only silence amongst the bodies. Rain solidifies as it falls.
Flowing backwards, evaporating, converging.
A red-black sun rises into the sky, obscuring its white counterpart.
A bloodless complexion emerges from the black sun, not a speck of blood on it.
He descends from the black sun.
I avert my gaze.
Am I afraid?
How shameful...

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: Hmm.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: You should not have dodged.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: The paleness of your face would have contrasted well with the blood drops.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: They would have painted a picture of beautiful despair.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Leeches can't stop playing with blood, I see.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Nothing has changed with you people, even after all these centuries.

a.text: Rain begins to fall again.
Drip. Drop.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: Look.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: It's a good day to die.

steps.name: Swordguard
steps.text: Your Grace, this attack was planned.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: As expected.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: For a sovereign of the Sarkaz to pay a personal visit, though... all well and good, I suppose.

steps.name: Swordguard
steps.text: The battle below is not going well. The officers are organizing the defense.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: No matter. This one is our only threat.

a.text: Mother... the Duke of Windermere points her sword towards the invading Sarkaz leader.
I cannot see the expression on her face, but I know that is not the mother I know so well.
The soldier was right. I would only be in the way.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: I've long had enough of Leithanian Spire Arts.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: I wonder what the spine of a Vampire looks like.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: Hmmm.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: You're a strong Victorian. You don't think you'll shirk back.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: But your blood will betray you.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: The creator built a bridge of life for humanity, and I stand above the bridge.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Not any worse than those spire madmen.

a.text: A blue blade cuts through the rain of blood.
A tiny drop of rain cuts open Mother's cheek.
Was it the red rain, or blood seeping out? I could not see.
There is no change in Mother's expression, but... have I ever seen her get hurt before?

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: Poor fool.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: Still clinging to dreams and fantasies.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: Guess why your battleship fell from within?

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Focus on the mission at hand, soldiers.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Ready.

steps.name: Swordguard
steps.text: Roger.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Your duty is to kill the enemies of Windermere, not protect the life of Windermere.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Do all you can to weaken the Sarkaz. Victoria will take back what is hers.

a.text: The Vampire's movement starts to slow.
No, the Swordguards are too fast.
I've received formal military training. I did not go to Londinium unprepared.
But here and now, I realize the weight of the words 'Duke of Windermere'.
My mother never let her daughter see the kinds of battlefields that she knew.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: Hm.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: Not bad, not bad... you aren't a duke of Victoria for nothing.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: How many Sarkaz have you eaten?

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: I don't have any such disgusting habits.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: You and your ancestors reveled in war, from Kazimierz to Leithanien.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: A Duke of Windermere once had an army of Sarkaz. In the War of the Four Nations, which engulfed most of the land...

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: How did you or your ancestor use them?

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: Parlor tricks, the theft of witchcraft, a favorite of the Nachzehrer.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: The blood and flesh of Sarkaz spread across the battlefield, becoming yet another bulwark for your glorious armada.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: You ate them up, alright.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Are you after revenge, Sarkaz?

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: How dare you trifle with the methods of my creation, the property of the Crimson Court?

steps.name: Swordguard
steps.text: He's being strengthened by the blood of the fallen?

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: It is no longer bodily fluids, but a part of the curse.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Prepare counter-Arts.

a.text: Stay calm.
Take a deep breath.
My throat is coarse. I cannot speak. I try to gasp for air, but the smell of blood is all there is.
Vampire and... Confessarius.
This is Mother's flagship. Lynncardine's most experienced commanders, bravest sailors and most steadfast warriors are gathered here.
Mother once told me that war is not about heroes, about charging into danger. A commander must see the whole battlefield, in order to see the way to victory.
But—
I realize why this ship sailed deep behind enemy lines without support.
Because of me.
No...
This is no time for self-flagellation.
I have to do something. If there is no place on Mother's battlefield for me... someone must bring order.
One of the Kings of the Sarkaz Court is here. But would they really attack us so recklessly?
My espionage background tells me that something is missing from this puzzle.
I have to do something.
Think!

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Could it be...? No, Arts that can teleport an entire army are unheard of... our ship fell from within...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I know this feeling...

a.text: Damazti.
I encountered him personally when leaving Norport. I had heard about this terrible King of the Sarkaz Court from Amiya. But he was defeated. How could he...?
Still, this is the most likely answer.
There are two Kings of the Sarkaz Court on this ship.
A truly terrifying conclusion.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: But what about the Vampire? Why didn't he go straight to his target, if he could use his witchcraft on the officers?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Attacking secondary targets with witchcraft, then creating disorder with assassins... that's too inefficient.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: But the Sarkaz fighting with Mother...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: The Damazti... did he simply infiltrate us by taking the face of a Victorian?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: If...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: —Damn it!

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Mother!

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Delphine?! Stay back—

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: That one's fake!

a.text: The Swordguards' weapons impale the Vampire.
The light of Arts penetrate the Sarkaz's twisted visage. The Arts of the Swordguards of Windermere, passed down from generation to generation, are simple, but brutally effective.
Mother quickly sets her sights back on the target.
I draw my sword.
The Swordguards do not hear my cry, but Mother is ready.
The Vampire laughs.
The massive Blood Arts explode before it can be cast.
A gust of wind sweeps through the sticky air, blowing away the sanguine rain and wind.
Death falls silent. True terror begins to spread, slowly but surely.
Blood converges upon the hand of the silhouette, forming a crystal. Then...
The other, the true—

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: Enough.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: I don't enjoy seeing another wear my face.

a.text: The Swordguards pull back instantly.
Even so, two of them are late by an eyelash, and their flesh takes incomprehensible form in a split second.
I can feel my sword hand trembling, my throat seizing up. This is a battle beyond my comprehension.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: A little girl saw through your disguise.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: You're losing your touch, Damazti. The previous you would have been more convincing.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Is that so?

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: These Arts are merely a poor imitation by the Confessarius.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: Foul, uncouth, vulgar killing.

a.text: He looks towards me, then towards Mother.
I'm trembling.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Delphine.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Y-Yes!

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Good job seeing through the trick. All the Swordguards would have been lost.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: But there's nothing more you can do here now.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I, I—

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: The escort fleet is approaching. We must ensure that communication with the fleet is maintained.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: The communications tower... it's behind the deck!

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: The enemy is few in number. Go.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: ...I'm counting on you.

a.text: She pats my shoulder with an injured hand.
Only then do I notice that she has many more scars on her than I remembered.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Understood.

a.text: I turn around and run for the communications tower.
Pride overcame fear in that instant. Mother said, 'I'm counting on you.'
I see the Confessarii trying to blow the communications tower, and our soldiers still resisting.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Thank goodness, the communications tower hasn't fallen yet—

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: The ship's slowing down?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: It's the engines! They're attacking the engine room!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: D-Damn it!

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Grab my hand!

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Don't look back! Get up!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Thank you! Oh, L-Lady Delphine—

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: We must regroup and counterattack. Reinforcements are on the way.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Listen up, men!

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Dust clouds in the distance! Help is on the way!

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Their plan—

a.text: Has failed? So easily?
I turn around.
The front of the deck has been completely engulfed in red fog, with only the flashing of sword and vampiric Arts to penetrate it.
Why do I feel so uneasy?
I—

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Delphine! Look out!

a.text: A pair of eyes peer at me, in the infinite raindrops, in the reflection of blood on the deck.
The Vampire's hand brushes my neck. Why? Is he not fighting Mother?
Vina tries to push me away, but it's too late.
My sword. I still have my sword.
I am her daughter.
She is counting on me.
The blood-woven crimson witchcraft vanishes into thin air.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: *Pant*... *pant*...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Are you alright?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I'm fine... it's all in my head...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Your troops are holding back the enemy down below, so we've come up to help.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: The bad news is that we found traces of the Damazti down there.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: We know. The Sanguinarch and Damazti are attacking together.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: No, wait...

a.text: That attack was not a Damazti feint. It was true blue vampiric witchcraft.
If the King of the Sarkaz Court had intended to kill me, there is no reason I should still be alive.
It was not my own strength that allowed me to resist.
He had other plans. There's no doubt about that.
Once again, I look towards the Swordguards. Their swords are still flashing. I can faintly see their silhouettes converging—
Something's not right.
They are falling, one by one.
They're backing up?
This is not right!
Where is Mother?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Delphine? Where are you going?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Agh, dreadful!

steps.name: Confessarius Guard
steps.text: (In Sarkaz) The scent of blood has changed. The Confessarius has succeeded, as has the Sanguinarch.

steps.name: Confessarius Guard
steps.text: (In Sarkaz) Pull back.

steps.name: Confessarius Guard
steps.text: (In Sarkaz) Those unable to do so, drive your daggers into your hearts on my command.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: You—

a.text: Impossible.
Even if the fight against the fake Vampire had taken its toll, Mother and her Swordguards could not have fallen so easily.
I know the legends of Windermere's sword which no wall could stop, the blade of light that struck down the spires, one of Victoria's two sharpest swords.
I grew up listening to them.
Why? How?
I charge into the fog of blood, hearing only my accelerating heartbeat.
Finally, I spy a figure.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: You have lost all sensation in your arms. Your guards are routed.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: How do you feel now?

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Argh... ugh...

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Sarkaz...

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: He caught you.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: An instant of weakness, of disorder... why? We do not understand.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: We find it... regrettable.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: She's finished. Let this great warrior savor the fading of life.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Are you leaving?

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: I have no interest in the inconsequential deaths that remain.

a.text: One glance from that devil is enough to freeze my blood.
But he does not kill me.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: This blood is a penny a gallon.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: What are you after? We are unsure.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: The age of shame is coming to an end.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Are you hurt?

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: ...It does not matter.

a.text: He disappears into the blood.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Y... You...

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Oh, there you are.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: The one who saw through us.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: He said we were losing our touch. How convincing was the last one?

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Is this good enough?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Don't—you dare—wear her—face—

a.text: He smiles at me with Mother's face.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: ...We must try.

a.text: Then, with an identical sword—Mother's sword—
He impales his own chest.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Sarkaz!

a.text: In my fury I try to charge, but my body refuses to move.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: (In Sarkaz) We'll do better next time.

a.text: He whispers in my ear, wearing my own face.
Mother's sword is still in his chest.
In 'my' chest.
He falls, then familiar blood witchcraft covers him, consuming him.
After the blood boils and evaporates, it is as though nothing had ever happened.
All I can do is pick up Mother's sword.
I catch sight of Mother.
The sound of fighting has stopped. The wind has calmed. The ship has stopped.
I see blue hair on the ground. Mother is bleeding.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Delphine...

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: I can't see very well...

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Have they retreated?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Mo...ther...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: They're gone...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Mother... I, I'll call for the doctors—

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: You'll be fine. You're the Duke of Windermere. You're my mother.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Wait here, I'll—

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: I couldn't beat him... I can't believe it...

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Don't go, Delphine... don't go...

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Let me... look at you...

a.text: Mother's body grows cold in my arms.
I dare not let go.
The sound of Mother's heartbeat fades further and further away.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Don't cry.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I... I'm not crying, Mother.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: I saw you swing your sword, Delphine... very good.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: You had injured your hand. Your grip... it was never right. I was too hasty.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Mother... don't say any more...

a.text: Mother gazes towards the horizon. Is that the direction of Londinium?
Her eyes have always lain upon Victoria.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: I remember... the direction your father left in...

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: We had a surprise for you... one that we prepared long ago...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Mother...

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Delphine, you—

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: I thought you would be taller... the clothes will be a bit loose...

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Just... calm down, Delphine...

a.text: The rain stops.
